messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT CREATED — KV-cache continuous-batching spike detected in prod (region: us-west1). Error rate + tail latency rising on Llama and Mistral endpoints. Pager routed to oncall (emma). auto-assign:emma

emma: seeing 5xxs and very long token latency from cont-batch workers. heatmap shows sudden kv-cache cardinality growth around 14:02. impacted models: llama-2-13b, mistral-instruct-v0, qwen-v1-mqa. rolling errors line up with a change in batching window on the routing tier.

ryan: copying logs — starting tail for shard hot-ops. `kubectl -n inference logs -l app=contbatch -f --since=10m`

kai: graph link: https://grafana.redwood/incident/2909999999 — prefix-cardinality line spikes dramatically. prefetch hit rate down, eviction thrash up.

emma: customer-facing: a handful of high-volume tenants seeing 5x latency for generation calls. cs-bot, can we surface impacted customers?

cs-bot: Alert: customers AtriaHealth, NoteBox, and SalesLoop flagged increased error rates. ETA for automated customer notif: 15m unless mitigated.

liz: quick hypothesis: MQA workload combined with aggressive continuous batching window causing cache keys to explode due to prompt-prefix variability. GQA appears less affected but Qwen MQA variant shows KV churn.

raj: can we hotfix by narrowing cont-batch window and disabling prefetch for MQA models? safe to do across Dedicated?

emma: yes propose two-step mitigation: 1) throttle cont-batch window from 200ms -> 50ms for weight-sensitive models; 2) disable prefetch for known MQA variants (qwen-* and mistral-instruct-*).

ryan: running command to lower batch window on route policy:
```bash
redctl routes update --name contbatch --param batch_window_ms=50 --selector "model in (llama-2-13b,mistral-instruct-v0,qwen-v1-mqa)"
```

deploy-bot: queued config change `routes/contbatch` -> applying to us-west1 workers (canary first: 10%).

emma: rolling canary watching traces. if errors hold -> roll to 100%. patching prefetch in parallel with small blast radius.

kai: disabling prefetch for qwen/mistral models now:
```bash
redctl models update --model qwen-v1-mqa --prefetch enabled=false --reason "incident 2909999999"
redctl models update --model mistral-instruct-v0 --prefetch enabled=false --reason "incident 2909999999"
```

deploy-bot: model flags updated (canary applied to 12 pods).

ryan: immediate telemetry shows request 95p latency dropping after the batch_window change and prefetch disable. error rate down ~60% in canary.

liz: good sign. what about Llama prefix thrash? still some KV evictions high on shard-17.

emma: raj — can you take shard-17 and manually trigger KV eviction smoothing / force stabilization? command below.

raj: running smoothing script with caution:
```bash
ssh ops@shard-17
sudo /usr/local/bin/kvctl set-eviction-policy --shard=shard-17 --policy=gradual --drain-interval=30s
```

raj: applied. watching memory and eviction metrics. no immediate regressions.

cs-bot: customers updated: initial mitigation in place, engineers investigating root cause. AtriaHealth acknowledged and asking for ETA.

emma: next steps: preserve canary, monitor 15m, if stable roll changes cluster-wide. collect top-k prefixes that caused cardinality to spike and add to a temporary prefix-blocklist for aggressive caching.

liz: grabbing top prefixes now. will push a prefix denylist for 1h to reduce noise.

ryan: prefix denylist applied against cont-batch routing: `denylist_prefixes = ["/tmp/base64/", "user-session-id:"]` (applied to canary).

emma: metrics look stable across canary and early rollouts. errors down to baseline for Mistral, Qwen. Llama still 10% above baseline but improving after shard smoothing.

liz: root-cause hypothesis: recent optimizer change to continuous-batching (rolling rollout ~2h ago) increased aggregation window + changed prefetch key normalization. combo triggered an explosion in prefix variants for MQA-style prompts. will prepare rollback patch for the optimizer change and a targeted config patch to make prefetch key normalization idempotent.

raj: if we roll back optimizer, is there any perf regression we should worry about? costing tradeoffs?

emma: yes rollback will increase p99 latency slightly for benign workloads but prevents cache blowup. prefer safe fallback for next 24h.

ryan: kickoff rollback now for the optimizer change (canary). `deploy rollback contbatch-optimizer --to-revision v12`

deploy-bot: rollback started (canary -> 10% pods), monitoring health checks.

emma: good work. assigning action items: liz collect top-100 prefixes and upload artifact; raj run full eviction-sweep across affected shards after stabilization; ryan prepare postmortem timeline and include config diffs and command history; i'll coordinate customer comms. oncall handoff in 45m to kai.

kai: I'm taking followup for next shift. please add me to the incident bridge. joining now.

emma: handing off — oncall to kai for remaining monitoring and rollback verification. I'll remain available for customer sync. :thumbsup:

cs-bot: Customer notif: Sent interim update to AtriaHealth and NoteBox. Next update planned in 2 hours or on significant change.

emma: incident downgraded to mitigation mode. summary: cont-batch window narrowed, prefetch disabled on MQA models, optimizer rolled back to v12, shard eviction smoothing applied. continuing root-cause analysis and follow-up postmortem.

kai: acknowledged. I'll keep watch for 2h and escalate if we see renewed cardinality growth. logging handoff note to incident tracker.

emma: closing out active pager. everyone who pushed changes, please paste your commands into the incident ticket so ryan can assemble the timeline.

ryan: will do, grabbing logs and all command history now.

emma: :white_check_mark: incident mitigated — moving to postmortem stage.
